sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The government plans to double the standard length of time migrants must live in the UK to qualify for permanent settlement from five to 10 years. A 10-year pathway requires earning at least £12,571 for five of the seven years before settlement. Shorter qualifying periods of three or five years apply to specific groups, including high earners, certain care workers, skilled public service workers, and people with British National (Overseas) status. Conversely, migrants who claimed certain benefits or breached rules face a 20-year wait. Additional conditions include having no criminal record, speaking good English, owing no taxpayer debt, and having a record of National Insurance contributions.

gist: Cocaine has overtaken heroin as the leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales.
Figures show 1,233 cocaine deaths last year, with overall drug poisoning deaths remaining historically high.
Charities call for urgent government action as rising purity and availability drive fatalities.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Office for National Statistics figures revealed that cocaine caused 1,233 deaths last year, becoming the drug most involved in drug-related deaths at 22%. While total drug poisoning deaths fell slightly by 46 compared with the previous year to 5,519, cocaine-specific deaths are four times higher than a decade ago. Deprived areas and older users over 40 were particularly affected.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Charities described the statistics as a national scandal and a direct result of policy failures and government inaction. Surging consumption, record production in South America, and falling prices have combined with increasing purity to create heightened risks.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Campaigners are urging the government to launch a new drugs strategy with clear priorities and restore investment to support growing numbers of people in treatment and recovery services.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: US tech stocks recovered on Tuesday afternoon following a recent selloff that worried investors about artificial intelligence spending. The Nasdaq increased by 0.83% and the S&P 500 rose by 0.37% at market closing. Meanwhile, the Dow dropped 0.38% after Apple released a worse-than-expected margin forecast driven by higher memory chip costs. Nvidia and other chipmakers such as Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom and Micron Technology experienced gains on Tuesday.

sections.text: The market recovery ended a brief selloff that had pushed the Nasdaq into correction territory after dropping 10% from its 6 October record close. gist: Geoffrey Hinton warned humanity might have been better off without artificial intelligence.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Computer scientist Geoffrey Hinton warned that humans might have been better off never developing artificial intelligence. He predicted a large-scale incident, such as a temporary blackout of financial or power systems, could occur this year or next year. Hinton criticized tech leaders for prioritizing money over safety and stated he did not trust OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Hinton warned that humanity faces a choice between radical abundance or severe societal problems, including mass unemployment and societies being torn apart. He urged for mandatory testing and independent evaluation of frontier AI models, comparing the current release of technology without prior safety checks to the handling of thalidomide.

articles.title: Those Jeff Bezos hair transplant photos are very fake
articles.standfirst: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and actor Jason Statham have a distinctive feature in common: They're both famously bald, and that definitely hasn't changed in the last few days.

gist: Fake images of Jeff Bezos and Jason Statham with hair are circulating on social media.
The photos are edited or artificially generated, and original images date back to 2011 and 2023.
Such manipulated media exploits social media engagement and highlights poor AI labelling solutions.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Images showing bald figures Jeff Bezos and Jason Statham with substantial hair have spread across social media platforms like X, Threads, and Bluesky. Investigations using reverse image search confirmed these pictures are fake, tracing the original unaltered photographs back to 2023 and 2011.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Social media shitposters turn engagement into revenue by creating fabricated nonsense. Because generative AI tools make manipulation more accessible and platform labeling solutions struggle to flag fakery, users are easily misled by attention-grabbing content.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: With ongoing generative AI advancements, manipulated media will likely continue to fool people online as creators chase likes, reposts, and engagement.
